Vegas hosts Calgary tonight with the better numbers on both ends. VGK creates 3.49 expected goals per 60 and allows 2.45, while CGY sits at 2.93 for and 3.24 against. At five on five, VGK has taken 56% of the expected goals in its games and CGY 49%. The model's expected goals for tonight are VGK 3.59 and CGY 2.67.

Special teams add to the gap. VGK generates 0.85 power-play expected goals a game and allows 0.34 on the penalty kill, against 0.28 and 0.46 for CGY. CGY also takes 4.67 penalties a game, which keeps handing power plays to the other side, and VGK draws 4.75. In net, Dustin Wolf is the projected starter for CGY, sitting at -6.07 goals saved above expected this season (.839 save percentage) after -2.8 over 57 games last year. Carter Hart is the projected starter for VGK at +0.64 this season (.906) and -4.44 over 18 games last season.

Form tilts the same way. VGK is 4-1-0 in its last five with 54% of the expected goals, though it was outchanced in its most recent win over NSH. CGY is 1-4-0 with 48%, and its one win, 4-2 at ANA on Oct. 13, came with 62% of the expected goals. For VGK, the model likes Jack Eichel (34% to score, 38% for two or more points), Mark Stone (36% to score) and Mitch Marner (29% to score). Matt Coronato gives CGY its best shot at a multi-point night (16%).
